deities: Khatu Shyam Ji (Barbarika - grandson of Bhima, worshipped as a form of Krishna)
festivals: Phalguna (Phalgun) Mela - Phalgun Shukla Dashami to Dwadashi (February-March), the temple's biggest fair

history.dynasty: Traditional founding by Roop Singh Chauhan of Khatu; present structure largely 18th century (renovation by Diwan Abhay Singh, 1720, under the Marwar ruler), with modern expansions
history.period: Original temple ~1027 CE (traditional account); rebuilt 1720 CE; renovated in modern times
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: The temple is at Khatu village (popularly called Khatu Shyamji) in Sikar district, Rajasthan - documented as Khatu with 'Khatu Shyamji' as the town name; it is NOT in Sikar town itself. The temple enshrines the head (sheesh) of Barbarika, grandson of Bhima, whom Krishna blessed to be worshipped as 'Shyam' in Kaliyuga after Barbarika sacrificed his head before the Kurukshetra war. Traditional accounts say the buried head was discovered at Shyam Kund after a cow's udder spontaneously spouted milk there, and Roop Singh Chauhan (prompted in one version by his wife Narmada Kanwar's dream) built the first temple around 1027 CE; the idol was installed on the 11th day of the bright half (Shukla Paksha) of Phalgun. The structure was renovated in 1720 by Diwan Abhay Singh at the behest of Marwar's ruler, giving it its present Rajasthani-style form, and has since been repeatedly expanded. Today it is one of North India's most-visited pilgrimage sites, with devotees seeking fulfillment of wishes (many families keep Khatu Shyam as kuldevta). Coordinates are from map geocode of the temple.

name: Khatu Shyam Temple
town: Khatu (CSV town 'Khatu Shyamji' is the popular name of the same village; the town is Khatu in Sikar district, NOT Sikar city)
town_description: Khatu (popularly Khatu Shyamji) is a pilgrimage town in Sikar district in Rajasthan's Shekhawati region, about 80 km from Jaipur. It is one of North India's most-visited devotional centres, drawing millions of pilgrims each year to the Khatu Shyam Ji temple and the adjoining Shyam Kund, with guest houses, dharamshalas and eateries serving the yatra crowd.

travel.railway: Ringas Junction is the nearest major station; a dedicated Khatu Shyamji station also serves the town (verify distances).
travel.road: Well connected by road from Jaipur (~80 km) and Sikar (verify distances).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the Phalguna Mela (February-March) is the peak pilgrimage - extremely crowded, plan accordingly.
